Hi all,

See below for an R talk in the psych department.  I note this topic will also be covered in the last portion of June's Software Carpentry Bootcamp.

Noam

To: <pda...@ucdavis.edu>
Cc: <gdsto...@ucdavis.edu>, <xs...@ucdavis.edu>, <swe...@ucdavis.edu>, <zh...@ucdavis.edu>, <mich...@ucdavis.edu>, <jca...@lib.ucdavis.edu>, <crro...@ucdavis.edu>, <jlh...@ucdavis.edu>, <eduardo...@uam.es>, <ja...@ucdavis.edu>, <crca...@ucdavis.edu>, <che...@ucdavis.edu>, <ds...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: Listserv: Quantitative Brown Bag - Melissa McTernan - 05/08/14

Verification: Following message sent from dept listserv to: all faculty; all PSYCHOLOGY grads; 

Please join us Thursday at 1:30pm in Young Hall 166 to listen to Melissa McTernan give a talk on the following:

Title: A demonstration of basic Sweave skills for an APA style manuscript

Abstract: This talk will be two-fold. The primary goal will be to demonstrate the basics of using Sweave (a program that allows for literate programming in R using the LaTex language) to produce an APA style manuscript, including figures and tables. In line with this goal, I will be distributing handouts that will help a novice user get started with Sweave. In order to demonstrate these skills, I will walk through a simulation study that I have been working on that involves mean comparison tests and positively skewed data.


We hope to see you there!

Thanks,
Pega Davoudzadeh
Quantitative Brown Bag Coordinator

parts:
Sweave might be the right tool for the application the author has in mind, but I have the sense that knitr is superseding Sweave.  See, for instance:

    http://gforge.se/2012/08/getting-started-with-knitr-and-sweave/

And/or do a web search for "knitr sweave", etc.  In other words, if you're starting from zero, it might be better to focus on knitr.

-- Mike
